active_paradigms.idea: Joint maximin nonlinear program via scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP) with a slack variable and locked orientations
active_paradigms.description: Replace the coordinate-wise LP polish with a joint maximin nonlinear program over all 22 coordinates plus a slack variable t. Constraints: for each of the 165 triplets, s_ijk * D_ijk >= 2t, where D_ijk = x_i(y_j-y_k)+x_j(y_k-y_i)+x_k(y_i-y_j) is the double signed area and s_ijk is the sign of D at the current iterate ('orientation locking'), plus 33 linear membership constraints y>=0, y<=sqrt(3)x, y<=sqrt(3)(1-x); objective is minimize -t. Solve with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='SLSQP') supplying analytic gradients (dD/dx_i = y_j-y_k, dD/dy_i = x_k-x_j) — 23 variables and ~200 smooth constraints solve in well under a second. After each solve, re-lock the signs from the new layout and warm-start a re-solve, repeating until signs stabilize (typically 3-8 rounds). This strictly generalizes the existing _lp_polish (which is exactly this program restricted to one moving point) and escapes the single-point-optimal stagnation that currently caps the pipeline, because all 11 points move together. Run this joint solver on every seed and every basin-hopping incumbent within the ~220 s budget, keep the best-ever layout, and optionally precede each solve with a short log-sum-exp soft-min continuation (tau shrinking from 0.01 to 0.0005) to smooth the landscape.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary) — escape single-point-optimal local minima via simultaneous multi-point moves; push combined_score from 0.874 toward and past 1.0 while keeping eval_time under ~220 s
active_paradigms.cautions: If a triplet's signed area approaches zero the locked-sign program can become infeasible — on any solver failure keep the incumbent and continue. Scale areas by 1/(2·triangle area) so constraint values are O(0.03) and coordinates O(1) for SLSQP conditioning. Never trust the solver's reported t; always recompute the exact min area with the evaluator's own formula and clip final points into the triangle with margin well above the 1e-6 tolerance. Keep the existing try/except fallback so any scipy failure still returns a valid configuration.

active_paradigms.idea: Symmetry-reduced parametric layout families searched globally with scipy.optimize.differential_evolution in ~8-12 dimensions
active_paradigms.description: Collapse the 22-dimensional search space to roughly 8-12 parameters by expressing layouts as unions of symmetry orbits of the triangle's D3 group, then run a true global search in the reduced space. Family A (mirror symmetry about x=0.5): apex vertex + base vertex pair + 4 mirror pairs (x, 1-x), giving 8 free parameters. Family B (C3-rotation core plus asymmetry): 3 vertices + one 3-point edge orbit (parameter t) + one 3-point interior orbit (radius r, angle theta) + 2 free points, about 8 parameters. Family C: all 11 points on the boundary with staggered mirror-symmetric edge parameters. A parameter vector is evaluated by materializing the 11 points and computing all 165 triplet areas in one vectorized numpy expression (tens of microseconds), so scipy.optimize.differential_evolution (seeded, bounded, polish=True) can afford 1e5+ evaluations inside the time budget; dense multi-start Nelder-Mead is a cheap alternative. Feed the best symmetric layouts into the existing full-space LP/greedy polish to allow controlled symmetry breaking, since the true optimum may be slightly asymmetric. This reaches highly structured near-optima that perturbation-based restarts from random layouts essentially never discover, at a fraction of the dimensionality.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary) — reach structured high-quality basins unreachable by random-restart local search; combined_score above 1.0; eval_time stays low because reduced-space evaluations are extremely cheap
active_paradigms.cautions: Symmetric layouts can contain exactly collinear triplets (mirrored pairs together with axis points) giving zero area — initialize parameters away from known degeneracies and let the objective push them apart. Enforce parameter bounds so every materialized point is strictly inside the triangle (or clip after materialization). Always follow the reduced-space search with a full 22-dimensional polish, since the true optimum likely breaks symmetry slightly. Deduplicate points that coincide under the parametrization and use fixed seeds for determinism.

active_paradigms.idea: Ruin-and-recreate large neighborhood search with vectorized optimal point reinsertion (scipy.spatial.Delaunay candidate generation)
active_paradigms.description: Introduce a relocation move class the current pipeline completely lacks: teleporting points to the globally best position instead of nudging them by small steps. Loop: (1) remove the 1-3 points participating in the currently smallest-area triangles (or a small random subset); (2) build a reinsertion candidate set — a dense grid (~150x130 over the triangle) plus centroids and circumcenters of the Delaunay triangulation of the remaining points (scipy.spatial.Delaunay) plus dense edge samples, since optimal Heilbronn layouts are boundary-heavy; (3) score all candidates at once with numpy broadcasting: for candidate x compute the minimum over all pairs (i,j) of remaining points of the double area of triangle (x, p_i, p_j), and take the argmax — this is exactly the best min-area achievable by inserting one point; (4) refine the top few candidates with the existing single-point LP polish and accept the best if the exact min area improves (occasionally accept ties for diversification). Also use the same insertion machinery constructively: grow from 4 to 11 points by optimal insertion with a full polish after each growth step, producing diverse structured seeds for the other stages. Relocation jumps across basins that coordinate descent cannot cross and directly attacks the bottleneck triangles; each iteration costs ~1-2 ms, so thousands of iterations fit comfortably in the budget.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: min_area_normalized (primary) — escape local optima via large discrete reconfiguration moves that directly eliminate worst triangles; combined_score above 1.0; eval_time secondary (each LNS iteration is milliseconds)
active_paradigms.cautions: The insertion field ignores triangles formed among several newly inserted points — when reinserting multiple removed points, insert them sequentially and recompute the field after each insertion. Include boundary candidates or the search will miss boundary-optimal layouts. Recompute the exact min area with the evaluator's formula after every accepted move rather than trusting the field value. Keep deterministic RNG seeds, enforce a hard time deadline, and always retain the global incumbent so any failure degrades gracefully.
